findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a pytest group reports an assertion failure, then a later test hangs until the job is cancelled or times out.
Forge's test command uses `-q` (`forge.toml:6`), so pytest can report the failed test as `F` while deferring its traceback until the session ends ([pytest output documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/en/latest/how-to/output.html)). If the job ends before that summary, `_product_failure` does not recognize the failure marker, and `_restart` accepts the cancellation or timeout and reruns the job. A transient assertion can then pass on retry and leave CI green. The cancellation proof in `tests/test_ci_retries_failed_test_jobs.py:60` supplies a complete `AssertionError` traceback, so it misses this case.
